Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drug Company (MCCPDC), doing business as Cost Plus Drugs, is an American public benefit corporation, founded in 2022 with its main headquarters located in Dallas, Texas. The company is focused on the pharmacy distribution of drugs with a stated goal to lower the prices for generic drugs by removing middlemen, such as pharmacy benefit managers and by moving to a cost-plus pricing strategy. Cost Plus Drugs was launched in January 2022. It was co-founded by radiologist Alex Oshmyansky and billionaire Mark Cuban. According to Cuban, in 2018, Oshmyansky contacted Cuban with an email titled "cold pitch" in which he asked Cuban to invest in a pharmacy he envisioned to manufacture generic drugs and skip the middleman wholesalers. The company has said that the intermediary layer of the pharmacy benefit managers is typically responsible for the heavy markup that drugs see between the manufacturers and the customers.

The company originally used Truepill Pharmacy to fill prescriptions, but later transitioned to HealthDyne. Prices are direct to consumer, without any need or role for insurance. Oshmyansky is the founder and CEO. As of February 2022, the company was in the process of constructing a 22,000-square-foot (2,000 m2) factory in Deep Ellum, Dallas, for the purpose of manufacturing drugs in-house, which is scheduled to open in the 4th quarter of 2022. As of June 2022, the company had a selection of over 100 generic drugs, and by March 2023, over 350 drugs were available. In December 2023, the company had over 2200 drugs available. ## Tier 1: Absolute Cheapest

**Walmart $4/$10 Generics**
The floor for covered drugs. $4 for 30-day, $10 for 90-day on a set list (metformin, lisinopril, some hormones, common antibiotics). No card, no account, just cash at the counter. **Cost Plus Drugs (costplusdrugs.com)**
Drugs sold at cost plus 15% markup, a $5 pharmacy service fee, and $5.25 shipping. Ships to all 50 states. No insurance needed, no membership. For generics specifically, this frequently demolishes everything else. They have over 1,000 of the most highly utilized generic medications and growing. You upload or transfer your script, they mail it. Cost Plus Drugs also has a partnership with Alto Pharmacy, which operates in Austin and provides same-day pickup and delivery options locally.

---

## Tier 2: Free Discount Cards (Stack These)

Run your drug through all of these before filling — prices vary by pharmacy and by day, and none of them cost anything:

**SingleCare** — savings ranged from 85% to 99% off retail price on tested medications. Consistently beats GoodRx on generics in head-to-head tests.

**America's Pharmacy** — no limit on uses, whole household can use the same card. Often competitive with SingleCare, worth a second price check.

**GoodRx** — accepted at over 70,000 pharmacies including CVS, Walgreens, and Walmart. Widest network, not always cheapest. Prices quoted on the website can differ from what the pharmacy actually charges with an existing card number, so if you have an old GoodRx number, it may price differently than a fresh lookup.

**GoodRx Gold** ($9.99/mo individual, $19.99/mo family) — paid tier that beats the free card on some medications. Only worth it if you fill regularly and can confirm savings on your specific drugs exceed the fee.

**Texas Drug Card** (texasdrugcard.com) — uses lowest price logic, guaranteeing you pay the lower of a discount off Average Wholesale Price, MAC pricing, or pharmacy promotional/retail price. Free, Texas-specific, worth running alongside GoodRx.

---

**Script Unlock (scriptunlock.com)** — 122+ local pharmacies bid against each other for your prescription; Austin patients save an average of 66% off retail. Newer platform, no account required, free to use as a patient.

**RxLess** — another free discount card, accepted at Walgreens and CVS locations in Austin, quotes up to 88% savings on some drugs.

**NeedyMeds / RxAssist / Partnership for Prescription Assistance** — databases of 5,000+ patient assistance programs searchable by medication; most major drug companies — Novo Nordisk, Lilly, Pfizer, AbbVie — have dedicated assistance programs with eligibility typically requiring household income below 200–400% of the Federal Poverty Level and no existing prescription drug coverage for the medication. If you qualify income-wise, these can get drugs free or near-free directly from the manufacturer.

---

## The Actual Strategy

1. Look up your specific drug on **Cost Plus Drugs first**. If it's there, that's almost certainly your floor for generics.
2. If it's not on Cost Plus, run it through **SingleCare** and **America's Pharmacy** simultaneously and compare.
3. Check **Walmart's $4 list** if it's a common generic.
4. For brand-name drugs without generics, go straight to the **manufacturer's patient assistance program** via NeedyMeds.
5. **HEB Pharmacy** (Austin-native chain) frequently has competitive cash prices on generics that beat the national chains even before applying a discount card — worth checking directly.

The single biggest mistake people make is going to Walgreens or CVS without a card and paying retail. Any card, even the weakest one, will cut that significantly.
